rationale: The employer uses a hazardous solvent and introduces it into employees' work area, where employees have not previously been trained on its hazards. It must provide effective information and training when the new chemical hazard is introduced, with the specified training topics. Because employees will decant the solvent into workplace containers, those containers must be labeled, tagged, or marked. The employer must also maintain a written hazard communication program addressing labels, safety data sheets, and employee information and training.

The technician is an employee newly assigned to work in an area involving hazardous chemicals. The employer must provide effective hazardous-chemical information and training at initial assignment, including required hazard, protective-measure, program, label, and safety-data-sheet content. The employee must also be informed of applicable requirements, hazardous-chemical operations in the work area, and the location and availability of the written hazard communication program.

Because the covered process has a significant equipment and technology modification that is not a replacement in kind, the employer must use written management-of-change procedures. Before the change, those procedures must address the technical basis, safety-and-health impact, operating-procedure modifications, time period, and authorization requirements. Before highly hazardous chemicals are introduced and production is restarted, a pre-startup safety review must confirm conformity with design specifications, adequate safety/operating/maintenance/emergency procedures, completion of management of change for the modified facility, and completed training for each employee involved in operating the process.

Because PSM applies and the near miss could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic toxic release at the covered process, the employer must investigate the incident. The supplied facts do not establish an employee fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation, loss of an eye, or a recordable injury or illness; therefore the cited OSHA reporting and recordkeeping provisions are not triggered on this record.

Because the establishment is required to keep Part 1904 records and had 300 employees, it must create the annual summary, post it conspicuously without alteration, and electronically submit information from OSHA Form 300A. The supplied context states that the posting must begin no later than February 1 of the following year and remain through April 30. The OSHA 300 Log, any privacy case list, annual summary, and OSHA 301 Incident Reports must be retained for five years after the covered calendar year.

The described servicing work is within the supplied lockout/tagout context, and the approaching anniversary triggers the requirement to conduct a periodic inspection of the energy-control procedure at least annually to ensure the procedure and standard requirements are followed.

The described jam-clearing is covered servicing under §1910.147, and unexpected startup or release of stored pneumatic energy could cause injury. Before servicing, the employer's energy-control program requires the machine to be isolated from its energy source and rendered inoperative. Documented energy-control procedures must be developed and used. After lockout or tagout devices are applied, stored or residual pneumatic energy must be relieved, disconnected, restrained, or otherwise rendered safe.

The contractor is being selected for work in a covered process area, which triggers the host employer's duty to obtain and evaluate the contractor's safety performance and programs. Because contractor employees will enter the process area and face known fire, explosion, and toxic-release hazards, the host employer must communicate those hazards and implement safe work practices controlling contractor entry, presence, and exit. The contract employer must ensure each contract employee is instructed on relevant job/process hazards and applicable emergency-action-plan provisions. A contractor employee injury and illness log related to the contractor's process-area work must also be maintained.

The requester is a former employee seeking the OSHA 301 Incident Report describing that former employee's own injury. The employer maintains the requested report and is covered by federal OSHA recordkeeping rules. The employer must provide a copy containing that information by the end of the next business day.

Because an authorized employee representative requests OSHA 301 Incident Reports for an establishment where the representative represents employees under a collective bargaining agreement, the employer must provide the reports within 7 calendar days. The copies may contain only the OSHA 301 section titled "Tell us about the case"; all other information must be removed.

The employee death resulted from a work-related incident. The fatality must be reported to OSHA within eight hours. Because it is a new, work-related case at a recordkeeping-covered establishment and death meets the general recording criteria, it must be recorded on the OSHA 300 Log and OSHA 301 Incident Report within seven calendar days of receiving information that the recordable injury occurred.

The work-related incident resulted in both an employee amputation and in-patient hospitalization. The employer must report the event to OSHA within 24 hours. Because the case is stated to be recordable and the employer learned of it today, it must be entered on the OSHA 300 Log and OSHA 301 Incident Report within seven calendar days of receiving that information.

The new-employee orientation is supported by the requirement to inform each employee of the procedure for reporting work-related injuries and illnesses. The supervisor's threatened discipline following a work-related-injury report is inconsistent with the prohibition on discharging or discriminating in any manner against an employee for reporting, and may also render the reporting procedure unreasonable if it would deter or discourage accurate reporting.

Because the process is covered by federal OSHA PSM and the organization is conducting the required three-year compliance audit, it must certify that it evaluated compliance at least every three years to verify that PSM procedures and practices are adequate and followed. For each audit finding, it must promptly determine and document an appropriate response and document correction of deficiencies.

The scheduled inspection of covered-process equipment triggers documentation of the inspection and application of the equipment-deficiency requirement. Because the vessel is outside acceptable limits, it must be corrected before further use unless necessary means are taken to assure safe operation while correction occurs in a safe and timely manner. Determining whether continued operation can be made safe requires qualified engineering and safety judgment.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Escalate to qualified process-safety/engineering personnel to determine whether the vessel must be removed from service before further use or whether necessary means exist to assure safe operation pending timely correction.

rationale: The employer uses the hazardous chemical in the employee's work area, so it must have a safety data sheet in the workplace. It also must ensure that required safety data sheets are readily accessible during each work shift to employees in their work areas, without barriers to immediate access. The reported inability to immediately access the sheet on the night shift is inconsistent with that accessibility requirement.

The portable container is filled from a labeled container, is intended only for the immediate use of the employee performing the transfer, remains under that employee's control, and is not stored. Therefore, the stated portable-container labeling exception applies; the employer is not required to label this portable container.

predicted_citations: Each lockout or tagout device shall be removed from each energy isolating device by the employee who applied the device.
rationale: The supplied OSHA excerpt establishes the default rule that the employee who applied the lockout or tagout device must remove it. The scenario proposes removal by another employee because the applying employee has left and cannot be reached, but the supplied context contains no exception, alternative-removal procedure, or conditions authorizing another employee to remove the device.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Whether an employer-specific, OSHA-compliant alternative lock-removal procedure exists and what conditions it requires is not supplied. The provided excerpt alone does not support authorizing another employee to remove the lock.

rationale: Because one employer's hazardous chemicals may expose another employer's on-site workers, the employer must have a written hazard communication program and must include methods for providing the other employer on-site access to safety data sheets for each hazardous chemical.

The proposed reactor-component swap is an equipment change in a PSM-covered process. Although replacements in kind are excepted from management of change, the maintenance records identify a different material specification and operating limit, and engineering and operations disagree about technical equivalence. If the component is not a replacement in kind, written management-of-change procedures apply and must address the technical basis, safety and health impact, operating-procedure modifications, change duration, and authorization before the change.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Qualified engineering/process-safety judgment is required to determine whether the different material specification and operating limit remain technically equivalent to the existing component or make this a non-in-kind replacement subject to management of change. The record should be resolved against applicable design/process-safety information before installation or use.

rationale: A 24-hour report is required only when an employee's in-patient hospitalization resulted from a work-related incident. The supplied facts establish a hospital admission after illness, but do not establish either work-relatedness or that the admission was in-patient hospitalization.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the illness resulted from a work-related incident and whether the employee was admitted for in-patient hospitalization. If both are true, report to OSHA within 24 hours after the hospitalization.

rationale: Federal OSHA requires effective information and training when a new chemical hazard that employees have not previously been trained about is introduced into their work area. Ordering a product alone does not establish that it is hazardous or that it presents a hazard not previously covered by employee training.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine from the product's hazard information whether it is a hazardous chemical and whether it introduces any chemical hazard on which the affected employees have not previously been trained.

rationale: The vendor is outside servicing personnel, but coordination under §1910.147(f)(2)(i) applies only when those personnel will engage in activities covered by the lockout/tagout standard. Coverage depends on whether the maintenance involves a machine or equipment for which unexpected energizing, startup, or release of stored energy could occur and cause injury. If that predicate is met, the on-site and outside employers must inform each other of their respective lockout/tagout procedures, and applicable energy-control procedures must be developed, documented, and used.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the planned routine maintenance exposes workers to potentially hazardous unexpected energization, startup, or stored/residual-energy release that could cause injury. The supplied facts do not establish that coverage predicate.

rationale: The establishment's 75 employees place it within the 20-249 employee range in §1904.41(a)(1)(i), and it keeps Part 1904 records. Electronic submission of Form 300A information is required only if the establishment is classified in an industry listed in appendix A to subpart E. The industry classification is not supplied.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: The establishment's industry classification, and whether that classification is listed in appendix A to subpart E of Part 1904, is required to determine whether electronic Form 300A submission is mandatory.
